verdict: This is the rare hackathon plan where the mandatory visual and the algorithmic core are the same object (the drawn route IS the objective), so nothing on screen is decorative: box colours come from opt-set pick counts, the cyan path comes from the grid Dijkstra predecessor map, the anneal animation is the real accepted-swap stream. All three 4.2 must-haves are met literally (top-120 satisfies "top ~100"; racks/aisles/dock/animated picker with live metres and seconds; swap-or-drag game with COI "fast movers nearest the dock" baseline), none of the three watch-outs is violated, and the honesty scaffolding (temporal held-out split, delta==full-recompute assertion, 200-random-layout context, single simulate() shared by worker/scene/eval) is better than anything else I would expect to see on the day. It is not yet a winner as written: the demo script shows the player LOSING to the 1963 baseline (You 32.7 vs COI 30.2) which deflates the game in front of judges; the "game mode" is a score button, not a game (no live score per swap, no target, no hint, no move budget) despite "game design" being a named skill in the brief; the SA story rests on numbers I do not believe (10-15k exact re-routings in 8 s in JS is 3-5x optimistic with ~100 affected orders per swap, and <2% of orders over 10 stops is optimistic for wholesale invoices averaging ~25 lines), the wall-clock SA budget makes the "seed 42 reproduces every number" claim false across machines, a warm-started high-temperature anneal will visibly get WORSE before it gets better on the live curve, and the 5-minute script carries ~12 interactions plus a 3x3 ablation matrix that a tired judge cannot absorb. The "where is the AI" question at an AI-branded hackathon is prepared but thin. Everything above is fixable in the next 3 hours without touching the architecture; fixed, this is an 8.5-9 and the deepest 4.2 entry in the room.
fatal_flaws: Reproducibility claim is false as designed: SA budgets are wall-clock (8 s live, 60 s eval) with a time-indexed cooling schedule, so seed 42 gives a different layout and km on a judge's laptop than in README; with 'fabricated results = disqualification' in the rules, a judge re-running `npm run eval` and getting different numbers is the one scenario that turns a strength into a DQ review. Must switch to iteration budgets (schedule indexed by iteration, time shown only as a measurement).

Illustrative numbers (41.9 / 30.2 / 32.7 / 27.x km) are embedded in the demo script and will leak into slides, posts and narration unless mechanically prevented; the pptx generator and README tables must read eval/results.json and nothing numeric may be hand-typed.
weaknesses: Demo shows the human losing to the baseline (You 32.7 km vs COI 30.2 km) at 2:05; the 'game' moment becomes 'the 1963 heuristic beats you', then the SA beats both; the player is a spectator.

Game mode is a SCORE button: no live score after each swap (the delta engine already makes this ~1 ms), no target line, no hint, no move budget, no win condition. The brief lists 'game design' as a required skill and this will be the thinnest part of the entry.

SA throughput claim (10-15k swaps in 8 s) is likely 3-5x too high: avg affected orders per swap is ~100-120 on an opt set of ~1,500 orders (top SKUs appear in 20%+ of invoices, frequency-weighted proposal makes it worse), mean Held-Karp cost per re-route is ~5-10k ops because of the heavy tail, so ~0.5-1 M ops/swap, ~2-3 ms, i.e. ~3-4k swaps in 8 s. On a 120! permutation space that is shallow; the live anneal may end ABOVE the COI line unless warm-started with low T.

Warm-starting the live anneal from COI with T0 = median|delta|/ln2 means the curve rises first (half of uphill moves accepted); judges see 'the AI makes it worse' for the first seconds. Either plot best-so-far as the bold line or start from a random layout so the curve crosses the COI markLine live.

The '<2% of orders with >10 covered stops' estimate is probably wrong: Nov 2011 has ~3,000-3,400 invoices and ~80k rows (~25 lines/invoice); with 20-30% coverage, mean covered stops ~5-7 but wholesale invoices of 100+ lines give 25+ stops; expect 5-15% of orders (and a larger share of total km) on NN+2-opt+Or-opt. The 'exact inner objective' claim then covers a minority of the distance.

SA optimises under exact routing but real pickers use S-shape; a layout tuned for an optimal router can be worse under S-shape. No cross-policy row (SA layout scored with S-shape) is planned; an OR judge will ask.

Demo script is overpacked: hook, swoop, SKU card, replay, routing toggle, 3 drags, SCORE, RACE, ANNEAL (8 s dead air), evidence panel with 3 tables + violin, batching toggle, 30 s of spoken limitations, QR. That is ~12 interactions and ~20 numbers in 5 minutes on a venue laptop; anything slow pushes the close past 5:00.

Data leakage in the UI: boxes coloured by 'pick frequency' and SKU card 'picks this month' use the whole month, so the player and the visual see the held-out half; COI must be computed from opt-set counts only and the UI must show opt/test counts separately or the held-out claim is cosmetic.

Explanation surface is wide for 4 humans in 17 h: R3F + drei (CameraControls, DragControls, Line2, Html, Instances) + zustand + motion + ECharts + Tailwind 4 + vitest + tsx + pandas. ECharts (~1 MB) and motion exist for one line chart and two counters; both are 40-60 lines by hand and fully explainable.

Version pins (vite 8.3.5, three 0.186.1, drei 10.7.9, R3F 9.8.2, motion 14.5.0, echarts 6.1.0, tailwind 4.3.3, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0) are unverifiable from here and a single wrong pin costs 20 min at 22:30; let `npm create vite@latest` + `npm i` resolve and record the lockfile.
Dark Tailwind theme + thin 3 px cyan line + small boxes on a washed-out venue projector is a legibility risk; no 'projector mode' planned.

Slot model is ambiguous: 120 SKUs in exactly 120 slots makes drag-to-empty-bay (as narrated at 1:35) impossible; it is swap-only. Decide 120 SKUs in 144 slots (24 empty, SA move set gains 'relocate') or narrate swaps only.

Commit history starts at 22:00, 4 h after kickoff; instructions say commit hourly from kickoff and that history is reviewed. Not disqualifying, but the gap needs a DEV_LOG entry and the repo should go up now.

S-shape test (S-shape >= exact) only catches an S-shape that is too SHORT; a buggy S-shape that is far too long inflates the 'exact routing saves X%' ablation. Add an upper sanity bound and a hand-checked 2-aisle, 3-stop case.

'Where is the AI' is answered with 'the metaheuristic is the AI'; at an AI-branded event with ML-heavy sibling tracks that is one sentence of exposure in Q&A with no data-science artefact to point at.
fixes: Make SA deterministic: budget = iterations, not seconds (live: N_live swaps chosen tonight so it takes <= 8 s on the demo laptop, e.g. 4,000; eval: 50,000 swaps x 5 seeds); geometric cooling indexed by iteration; display elapsed ms as a measurement only. README sentence: 'seed 42, 50,000 iterations -> identical layout on any machine'.

Turn the game into a game using the delta engine: after every swap the KPI tiles update live (opt and test km) within ~50 ms; add a target bar (Original -> COI -> SA), a 10-swap budget, an 'Affinity hint' overlay drawing lines on the floor between the top-10 co-picked pairs that sit > 8 m apart (computed from the opt set only), and an undo. SCORE becomes 'verify with full replay' (numbers identical to the live delta, which doubles as the delta==full assertion on stage).

Rewrite the player beat at 1:35-2:35: start from the COI layout, perform 3 pre-rehearsed affinity-guided swaps that beat COI on the held-out set by ~1-2% (pick them tonight from SA's early accepted swaps), then RACE ghost-COI vs player; then let a judge do one swap with the trackpad and watch the tiles tick. Never show the player below the baseline.

Measure ms/swap first (tonight, in eval/run.ts) and only then choose the live-anneal choreography: (a) start from random with high T so the bold best-so-far curve crosses the COI markLine live (best moment if it crosses within the iteration budget), else (b) start from COI with T0 = 0.2 x median|delta| so the curve only descends. Bold line = best-so-far, faint = current J, markLines = COI and SA(50k).

Print in prep meta: share of orders with > 10 covered stops and their share of total km; set DP cutoff n <= 12 for scoring/reporting (3.2 M ops, fine offline and for a 3k-order replay) and n <= 9 inside the SA loop; add one ablation number '2-opt+Or-opt gap vs exact on the n <= 12 subset = X%'. If X < 1%, say so proudly ('heuristic routing is within 1% of optimal here; exact is for proof, not speed').

Add the cross-policy row: SA-under-exact layout and COI layout each scored with S-shape and with exact on the test set (4 numbers, one table). This answers 'real pickers do not route optimally' in 5 seconds.

Cut the demo to 4 interactive beats and <= 8 numbers: REPLAY (path draws, counters), EXACT toggle (metres drop), 3 swaps with live tiles + RACE, ANNEAL; evidence = ONE 4-row table (Original/COI/SA/You x held-out km and s/order) with the in-sample column beside; limitations = a persistent 'Assumptions' chip plus one spoken sentence; batching, violin, routing ablation and congestion move to README and Q&A cards. Target close at 4:30 with QR; 30 s buffer for a slow laptop.

Held-out hygiene in the UI: colour boxes and compute COI from opt-set (1-15 Nov) pick counts only; SKU card shows 'picks 1-15 Nov | 16-30 Nov' as two numbers; the Data panel states 'everything the player sees comes from the first half'. Add a Spearman rank correlation of SKU pick frequency between halves (one number) as the data-science artefact that explains why held-out gains shrink.

Drop ECharts and motion: hand-rolled 60-line SVG line chart for the convergence curve (append a point every 250 iterations), rAF counter for metres/seconds, HTML tables for evidence. Keeps the bundle ~600 KB gz and removes two libraries from the 'explain every line' obligation. Hard LOC budgets: sim <= 900, scene <= 900, ui <= 900, eval <= 300; each agent ships docs/explain-<module>.md with the 5 questions a judge will ask about that file and their answers.

Push the public repo NOW (not 22:00): README skeleton, DEV_LOG entry '18:00-21:45 problem selection, data mirror verification, design', .env.example comment, LICENSE, download.sh. Then hourly commits on branches with a cron-style 45-min reminder.

Prepare the 'AI' slide as one line and one artefact: 'Search-based AI (simulated annealing over an exact Held-Karp objective) with an honest held-out protocol; no LLM by design: zero keys, zero cold start, every number reproducible from seed 42' + the Spearman drift number and the in-sample vs out-of-sample gap sentence.
steal_worthy: Temporal held-out split for an optimisation problem (decide on 1-15 Nov, score on 16-30 Nov) with the in-sample vs out-of-sample gap stated as a sentence generated from the numbers.

One pure-TS simulate() shared verbatim by the Web Worker, the 3D scene and the Node eval script, so README numbers and on-screen numbers are provably the same code; `npm run eval` as the single reproduction command writing results.md/json with commit hash and seeds.
Debug-mode assertion that every accepted incremental delta equals a full recompute (the test an OR judge asks for), doubled on stage by SCORE re-verifying the live tiles.

200 uniformly random layouts as a context distribution with the baseline/opponent/player marked as percentiles; immediately conveys how good any layout is without an 'original' that does not exist in the data.
Ghost-vs-player replay race on the same real invoice with diverging counters; the cleanest possible rendering of 'improvement is measured, not claimed'.
Self-drawing route from the grid predecessor map so the visual can never contradict the metric (the path cannot cross a rack by construction).
Q&A cards (20 s each) prepared in advance for the 8 predictable questions, with a named human owner per module and a 'who wrote which file' answer.
Declared-convention discipline: dataset has no layout, so 'Original' is a stated convention, walking speed and pick time are stated assumptions, with a sensitivity row (5/8/12 s per pick).
